claims.text: The initial alloy is an as-cast single-phase solid solution.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous chemical distribution.
Demanding mechanical loading can induce microstructural evolution in the initially single-phase alloy.
Thermal exposure near 700°C can cause an initially single-phase refractory HEA to segregate or form precipitates.
Oxygen and nitrogen interstitials can promote phase segregation during thermal aging.
Stress gradients make residual interstitial impurities mobile and promote localized segregation.
Minor inherent compositional fluctuations promote localized phase segregation under mechanical loading.
The induced segregation nucleates discrete precipitates or secondary phases.
The induced secondary phases are brittle intermetallic phases.
The precipitates preferentially form along grain boundaries and dislocation arrays.
The precipitates interrupt continuous plastic deformation.
The precipitates promote crack initiation and rapid crack propagation.
Stress-assisted segregation and precipitation cause a marked loss of fracture toughness or abrupt brittle fracture.
The as-cast baseline has uniformly high fracture toughness and ductile dimpled fracture morphology.
Loaded specimens will exhibit more secondary-phase formation than the as-cast baseline.
Loading will change the fracture morphology from ductile dimples to cleavage or intergranular brittle fracture.
Loaded specimens will show a significant reduction in measured fracture toughness.
The proposed behavior applies under high stress or high strain rate at temperatures where impurity mobility is appreciable.
At very low loading rates or under benign isothermal conditions, the single-phase state may remain stable.
The hypothesis is falsified if loaded specimens show neither increased segregation or precipitation nor a statistically distinguishable loss of toughness or ductility relative to the control.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as as-cast in one field but as initially homogenized in another; these are distinct processing states unless homogenization is being used only informally to mean chemically uniform.

The conditions field defines the main comparison as mechanically loaded specimens versus loaded specimens with added thermal aging, whereas the experiment defines the control as an unloaded as-cast specimen. It also calls for two sets while subdividing the loaded set into with- and without-thermal-exposure conditions, implying at least three experimental groups.
